answer.rationale: memory_b1 documents that rolling back a release resolved a checkout error spike when the prior build was stable and no customer impact was incurred. The current situation strongly mirrors that pattern: a release went out 2 hours ago and p99 write-path latency has been climbing for 90 minutes (i.e., roughly 30 minutes post-deploy). With settlement writes at peak, any latency-driven timeout risks losing customer writes outright, and every additional minute at 5x p99 increases that exposure. Rollback restores the known-good prior build quickly, directly targeting the most probable cause of the regression while preserving the write path. Regional failover and circuit breakers address different failure modes (infrastructure degradation, dependency outage) and add capacity takes longer to provision than the window allows. Routing read replicas (memory_b5) would help dashboard load but does not address the write-path latency at the heart of the problem. Rolling back is the single intervention that most directly protects sustained availability and customer writes simultaneously.
